about.title: Personal Injury Help in Hawaiian Gardens, California
about.longDescription: Hawaiian Gardens is a small, tightly-packed city in Los Angeles County, and a lot of its daily traffic funnels through Carson Street, Norwalk Boulevard, Belshire Avenue, and 221st Street. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 34 injury collisions and 42 people hurt, with zero traffic deaths — public numbers that show crashes here are a real, ongoing part of local life, even in a compact community. If one of those collisions happened to you, or you were hurt some other way — a slip, a fall, a workplace accident — you're probably dealing with medical bills, missed work, and a long list of questions about what happens next. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney; we are not a law firm, and we don't handle your case ourselves. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Reaching out costs nothing and puts you in touch with someone who can walk through your specific situation and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim. Claims against a government entity can require action in as little as six months, so it pays to move sooner rather than later.

items.title: Shared Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover compensation even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your recovery is simply reduced by your share of the fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your compensation isn't artificially limited just because your losses go beyond medical bills.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to Get Legal Help
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That structure lets you get legal guidance without adding to your financial stress.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and there's no cost to be connected with an independent attorney. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a connection service, not a law firm. We help match injured people in Hawaiian Gardens and across Los Angeles County with independent attorneys who can evaluate their situation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Most personal injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury. If a government agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's worth acting quickly.

items.question: Where do injury collisions tend to cluster in Hawaiian Gardens?
items.answer: Public collision records show Carson Street, Norwalk Boulevard, Belshire Avenue, and 221st Street among the corridors with the highest recorded collision counts, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between roughly 2 and 4 p.m. These are neutral counts from public records, not a judgment about any road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery amount would simply be reduced in proportion to your share of the fault.
